chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, did not create anything except that He intended it to be worshipped, and He did not create anything except that He intended it to be worshipped, and He did not create the heavens and the earth, the sun and the moon, except to be worshipped.
He said: And He created the jinn and mankind except to worship Him.
He said: So everything that was created is for worship.
ai.seo_question: What is the ultimate purpose of creation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidating that the ultimate teleological purpose of creation is *ibadah* (worship), which in Shia theology encompasses both servitude and recognition of divine authority. This narration anchors the cosmic order in the verse 'I did not create jinn and humans except to worship Me' (51:56), establishing that all existence, from celestial bodies to humanity, is oriented toward acknowledging Allah's sovereignty. This concept serves as the foundational principle for understanding the role of the Imams as the perfect exemplars of this worship and the means through which creation fulfills its purpose.
